verdict: Accept the deterministic direct-publication continuity rule for the 163 ordinary unique endpoint pairs, conditional on exact name/type/region bindings, exact selected-record IDs and values within the published thousand-person compatibility interval. This supports same-city identity continuity 2010↔2021; it does not admit coordinates or assert harmonized population scope.

sample.design: Fixed stratified review: six each from 2010 display bands <200, 200-499, 500-999, 1000+ thousand persons; cases fixed before verdict; raw Table 4.9 page/line and selected source endpoints checked.
sample.result: 24/24 direct row and unique endpoint bindings agree; city type, year, normalized region and published-thousand compatibility checks pass; no footnote markers.

rule_population.selected_endpoint_uniqueness: 163/163 unique source record in each year; no duplicate endpoints
rule_population.region_type: 163/163 same normalized region and city type across selected endpoints

held_cases.policy: No automatic admission: boundary-change/federal-city cases held; blank stays missing; Russian-census ellipsis for Crimea/Sevastopol is outside that census universe, not an unresolved matching failure or zero.

source_method: Printed page 90 identifies cities with population ≥100,000 and units thousand persons. Footnote 1 explicitly distinguishes census-date columns 2002-10-09, 2010-10-14, 2021-10-01 from Jan 1 estimates. Footnotes 2–3 disclose Balashikha 2015 and Moscow 2012 boundary changes. Exact census observations remain in separate selected sources.
rounding_limit: Publication gives values in thousands but does not specify rounding convention in cited note. Nearest-thousand ±500 compatibility is an operational check, not an asserted official rounding rule.
coordinates: No coordinate claims reviewed or admitted.
source_provenance: Archived official Rosstat yearbook PDF retrieved from Wayback Memento 2025-02-03 with normal TLS verification. This verifies archive retrieval and official URL lineage, not contemporaneous TLS at Rosstat origin.
